title: coral surface · volcanic eruption from beneath
input: pointer (orbit + click to trigger eruption burst)

coral.rules: differential-growth (repulsion + neighbor-spring + radial pressure), pre-warmed 600 steps, age-graded basalt→amber palette, sinks slightly with age (crustal depth)
coral.vent_ring: initial 24-vert ring at radius 2.2 leaves a clear gap at origin where the volcano emerges

volcano.emission: ring-buffer; base sin pulse ~80-220/frame + burst windows (auto-burst every 10s, click-burst on demand) ramping to 800-1200/frame
volcano.physics: cone-upward initial velocity (4.5-10 units/s, half-angle 0.30-0.55 rad), gravity -8.4, life 1.6-3.0s, killed when life expires OR y < -0.6
volcano.palette: white-hot → yellow → orange → red → soot, age-graded with size-falloff
volcano.intent: particles erupt UP through the gap left by the coral ring, arc under gravity, cool, fall back through the network — break the crust from beneath

notes: Direct response to user feedback: 'i like 7ea, could have a new version where volcano like particle broke out of it from beneath'. Two simultaneous systems share a scene: 7ea-style coral surface on the y=0 plane with crustal sink, and a volcanic emitter at the origin firing 25k cone-spread particles upward through the gap in the coral ring. Heat-graded eruption palette + gravity arc + soot end-state. Click triggers 1.8s burst on top of the steady auto-pulse.
